strategy.summary: Fade (or follow) the shape of the recent move, flat by the close. Price-path convexity (Gulen & Woeppel, JFQA 2025, Purdue) measures when a move happened inside a window: draw a straight line from the window's first close to its last, and see whether the path sagged below it (convex: an up-move came late) or bulged above it (concave: it came early). The paper finds high convexity predicts lower returns on daily data; everything here is intraday, so it is an extrapolation. A plain N-bar reversal runs alongside as the control.
strategy.formula: convexity = ((P1 + PN)/2 − mean(P1..PN)) / ((P1 + PN)/2); high z → short, low z → long

rules.label: Signal
rules.text: Over the last N closes: paper = the formula above; ATR gap = the same average line-minus-path gap ÷ ATR(14); max gap = the single largest line-minus-path gap ÷ ATR(14); control = (PN − P1) ÷ ATR(14), the plain N-bar return. Each is turned into a z-score against its own last 250 or 500 bars.

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: A fresh cross of z above +entry goes short; below −entry goes long, filled at the next bar's open. Quadrant: all = every signal (the paper); late = only fades of the window's net move; early = only trades with it. Optional: the net move must be at least 1 or 2 × ATR(14); an EMA(50) or EMA(200) trend filter (longs above, shorts below). No entries in the last 30 minutes; a signal while a position is open is dropped.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Time exit after N/2 or N bars at that bar's close, or hold to the session close; optional stop 1.5 or 2.5 × ATR(14) from the entry, live inside each bar. Anything still open is closed at the session's last close.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Long, short or both; one position at a time, never held overnight. As many whole ES contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

strategy.length_note: All lengths are in bars of the chosen bar size; the move and stop are in ATR(14).

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 186,624 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the signal was recomputed independently and each entry was a fresh cross on the right side with every filter met, no qualifying signal was skipped while flat, fills were never better than the market, nothing was held overnight. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 69,159 (69,159 on 15min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 116,249 (116,249 on 15min); 88,950 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: look-back N and the z-score history by ±20% (rounded, at least one bar), the entry |z| by ±0.25, an ATR stop by ±0.25 and the minimum net move by ±0.5 ATR ("no stop" has nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 67.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 1,003 versions formed 168 groups; 312 of the 319 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades. Not run yet: the finalists are frozen and waiting for this step.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (ES.v.0), 1-minute bars aggregated to 15 minutes. Rolls are back-adjusted so the roll gap is not treated as a price move. The ATR gap, max gap and reversal signals are point distances; the paper form divides by a back-adjusted price level, so its scale drifts slightly with the roll adjustment (the rolling z-score absorbs most of it).
Day session only: NYSE regular session 09:30-16:00 NY on NYSE trading days. Overnight Globex trading is not used and nothing is held overnight.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side (stops and wick entries too) and $2.50 commission per contract per side, including the session-close exit.
Windows (up to 96 bars) and the z-score history run over the day-session bars across days, so the overnight gap shows up as a jump between two closes inside a window. Positions never cross sessions.
The paper tested convexity on daily closes with 5- to 21-day holds. Every look-back here is intraday, so the whole grid is an extrapolation of the paper.

The reversal control is extreme almost only in the direction of its own move, so for it quadrant "late" nearly equals "all" and "early" rarely trades. Hold "N bars" equals "to close" once N exceeds the bars left in the session.
Each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the other families; the stop changes where the trade exits, not how big it is.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of bars with an open position.
Other strategy families were already selected on this market's 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is.
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
